merger_description:
Mitsui & Co., Ltd (**Mitsui**), via its wholly owned subsidiary SPC Blue Pty Ltd (**SPC Blue**), is acquiring a 15% interest in the Rhodes Ridge Joint Venture (**RRJV**) to the extent that it remains to be put into effect after 21 July 2026.

The ACCC provided a letter to Mitsui on 21 July 2025 in relation to its proposed acquisition of the 15% interest in the RRJV which had the effect, pursuant to section 189 of the of the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth) (the **Act**), that Division 2 of Part IVA of the Act would not apply to the acquisition if it is put into effect within 12 months. Mitsui considers that certain steps contemplated by the acquisition may remain to be completed after 21 July 2026.

Mitsui is a Japanese general trading company with seven operating segments: i) iron & steel products, ii) mineral & metal resources, iii) energy, iv) machinery & infrastructure, v) chemicals, vi) lifestyle and innovation, and vii) corporate development. It invests in Australian iron ore through minority interests in Pilbara joint ventures.

The RRJV is an unincorporated joint venture concerning undeveloped iron ore deposits at Rhodes Ridge in the Eastern Pilbara, Western Australia.

The RRJV is managed and operated by Rio Tinto subsidiaries and there is no current iron ore production from the RRJV assets.

Rio Tinto currently owns a 50% participating interest in the RRJV, and AMB Holdings Pty Ltd currently owns a 10% participating interest. Mitsui is separately acquiring a 25% interest in the RRJV through a separate transaction.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the ACCC has
considered the information provided with the notification waiver
application and had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of
the Act.
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers
that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening
of competition. In particular:
a. Mitsui’s share in the supply of iron ore and share in iron ore
reserves in Australia and globally is low
b. there are several alternative global suppliers that supply iron
ore and hold iron ore reserves in Australia and globally
c. the Acquisition is unlikely to result in any substantive change
in the control of the RRJV.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
